marks.gloss_en: (for Munbaz) if throughout the Torah, where the korban is no novelty, being unwitting of the korban counts as shegaga, then for the oath on a statement, where it is a novelty, all the more so
rather, is it not the Rabbis'?
מיתיבי: one who knows the oath is forbidden but not whether a korban is due is liable -- so for the oath, unwitting of the korban suffices
הא מני -- מונבז היא: the baraita is Munbaz's, and Abaye spoke for the Rabbis (= p_bar_shevua_kemunbaz)
the baraita: what is an unwitting oath on the past? -- if he said 'I know this oath is forbidden, but not whether a korban is due' -- liable
כי אמר רבי יוחנן היכא דאיכא כרת -- R' Yochanan's leniency is confined to karet prohibitions, and teruma carries none
Abaye: all agree that for teruma one is liable to the added fifth only if he was unwitting of its lav
'and the children of Israel shall keep the Shabbat' (Ex 31:16, singular): one observance for many Shabbatot
מנהני מילי -- ושמרו בני ישראל את השבת: one observance for many Shabbatot, hence one chatat for the one who forgot the essence of Shabbat
מנהני מילי -- ואת שבתתי תשמרו: one observance for each Shabbat, hence a chatat for each Shabbat for the one who knew its essence
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: 'and the children of Israel shall keep the Shabbat': one observance for each and every Shabbat
מיתיבי: 'he keeps one day for six' -- does it not mean he counts six and then keeps one?
לא -- it means he keeps one and counts six. [Attacked at 69b.5: אי הכי, it should have said 'keeps one day and counts six']
Rav Huna: one walking on the road or in the desert who does not know when Shabbat is counts six days and keeps one
and on that day let him die?! [The proposed answer -- two portions the day before -- falls to 'perhaps the day before was Shabbat' (h_shtei_parnasot), and the text goes on: אלא...]
Rava: each day he makes [by work] enough for his sustenance, except on that day
the second baraita: one walking on the road or in the desert who does not know when Shabbat is counts six and keeps one
Rava: if he knows the part of the day on which he set out, he may work that whole day
